title: Month-count adjustment left an uncertain rise in consecutive flood days at 69 US gauges in 2018-2025
abstract: We tested whether consecutive flood days changed beyond changes in monthly flood counts at 69 US tide gauges. We used complete NOAA daily minor flood flags for 2018-2025 from a verified campaign publication. Adjacent pairs per 100 flood days rose from 36.76 in 2018-2021 to 40.39 in 2022-2025. A reference that kept each station-month count fixed rose from 7.64 to 8.23. The change above this reference was +3.04 percentage points, with a conditional 95% whole-year bootstrap interval of -4.19 to +9.32. A two-year block check also included zero. Mean days per month-bounded run rose from 1.581 to 1.677, with uncertain change. The observed flood-day increase depended strongly on 2024. This is a short-record diagnostic of daily order, not a test of unchanged event dynamics or a physical cause. Selected complete gauges, four years per period, daily boundaries, reused threshold screening, and the reference assumptions limit inference. Exact daily inputs, source hashes, code, saved bootstrap draws, an independent count audit, a repeat run and a figure are supplied.

display.caption: Flood days and month-bounded runs at 69 complete-record gauges. The right panel shows changes from 2018-2021 to 2022-2025 and conditional 95% whole-year bootstrap intervals. The monthly-count reference preserves each station-month flood count and removes day order.
